## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For precomputed collections queried through Search, pace bulk refresh writes and monitor their write volume together with search replication lag; otherwise a refresh burst can increase staleness and potentially force rebuilding. This application to refresh jobs is an inference from the documented bulk-write failure mode. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/monitoring.md
- [statement] Increasing lag is a warning, but small steady-state lag is normal. During initial sync, the replication-lag metric is not meaningful; diagnose build progress, source throughput, and resource pressure instead. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/monitoring.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting.md
- [statement] Repeated initial-sync transitions are not uniquely evidence of an undersized oplog: MongoDB also lists recurring steady-state exceptions, mapping-driven heap exhaustion, and index corruption. Inspect the preceding log error before selecting a remedy. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost
- [statement] When mongot falls behind the retained oplog window, it can no longer recover incrementally and performs a full index rebuild. Oplog rollover, slow indexing, and downtime can produce this condition. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting.md
- [statement] Repeated re-sync is not sufficient proof of oplog exhaustion: MongoDB also lists transient steady-state exceptions, mapping-driven heap exhaustion, corruption, and expensive index definitions. Inspect the preceding error and oplog window before choosing a remedy. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/monitoring/recommended-alerts.md
- [statement] Debezium independently documents the same retained-history constraint for its MongoDB change-stream consumer: a purged resume position prevents resumption and can cause an invalid-resume-token failure depending on snapshot.mode. This supports the general CDC constraint, not mongot-specific recovery behavior. (low confidence) — https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB warns that some self-managed index builds can take days; Percona repeats this warning rather than supplying an independent benchmark, so days is a possible recovery case rather than a typical duration or SLA. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/backup-restore.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/
- [statement] For offload designs that refresh an indexed precomputed collection, budget separately for collection-refresh freshness and downstream search-index freshness. This is an architectural inference from asynchronous indexing, rather than a measured end-to-end freshness guarantee. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/monitoring.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/user-guide/mongodb-search
- [statement] A mongot filesystem snapshot can avoid rebuilding only while change-stream history can carry it forward. If the restored snapshot is older than retained history, mongot rebuilds from mongod instead of simply resuming incremental replication. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/backup-restore.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] mongot consumes mongod changes asynchronously through change streams; a successful database write does not imply that the search index already reflects that write. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/monitoring.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/user-guide/mongodb-search
- [statement] If mongot falls behind the retained oplog window, incremental synchronization is no longer possible and a full index rebuild is required; existing search data can remain queryable but stale during recovery. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/backup-restore.md
- [statement] A filesystem snapshot avoids rebuilding only while its replication position can still be advanced through retained change-stream history. An older snapshot can be immediately queryable yet require rebuilding to regain freshness. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/backup-restore.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/
- [statement] Oplog headroom and consumer throughput address different risks: a larger retained history gives mongot more time through pauses or write bursts, while additional indexing capacity or fewer expensive indexes addresses sustained inability to keep up. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting.md
- [statement] The mongot-doctor repository documents a diagnostic report combining change-stream lag, initial-sync activity, oplog window, JVM heap, Lucene merges, and index health. Its heuristic thresholds and claimed amplification factors are not validated rebuild-cost measurements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/Miccolomi/mongot-doctor · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost
- [statement] Debezium independently documents the underlying MongoDB CDC retention hazard: after an outage, a saved resume position can have aged out of the oplog, and connector recovery depends on snapshot configuration. This corroborates the retention constraint, not mongot-specific rebuild duration or recovery behavior. (low confidence) — https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost
- [statement] Full index rebuilds are computationally expensive and time-consuming; MongoDB documents that some self-managed index builds can take days. This is a possible recovery duration, not a typical or guaranteed rebuild time. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/monitoring.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/backup-restore.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
- [statement] Monitor replication lag against the oplog window and investigate growing lag together with write rate, CPU, and disk I/O. More retained history increases recovery headroom; additional indexing capacity or reduced write bursts addresses the rate imbalance. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/monitoring/recommended-alerts.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting.md
- [statement] MongoDB self-managed monitoring documents mongot_index_stats_indexing_replicationLagMs as a per-index metric in milliseconds. The metric family is absent before an index exists, so absence must not be interpreted as zero lag. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/monitoring.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/monitoring/recommended-alerts.md
- [statement] Search can remain available while a stale index rebuilds: Atlas documents stale results during oplog-triggered rebuilds, and restored self-managed snapshots remain queryable during rebuilding. Availability does not establish freshness. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/deployment/backup-restore.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
- [statement] Alibaba Cloud documents that restoring an ApsaraDB instance from backup does not restore search indexes; users must re-enable Search and rebuild them. This is a service-specific recovery rule and must not be generalized to Atlas or filesystem snapshots of mongot. (low confidence) — https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/user-guide/mongodb-search · keywords: mongot replication lag, oplog window and index rebuild cost
